name: Hadrian
summary: Automated manufacturing company building factories for precision parts.
overview: Hadrian uses automation and software to manufacture precision components for aerospace and defense.
bull_case: Software-defined factories can address domestic capacity and defense-supply-chain constraints.
bear_case: Capital requirements, manufacturing execution, and customer qualification cycles are substantial.

intelligence.description: Hadrian builds software-defined factories that manufacture precision parts, assemblies and systems for aerospace and defense customers.
company: Hadrian uses automation, software and vertically integrated factory operations to produce mission-critical components and systems for aerospace and defense.
Its factories-as-a-service model is designed to expand domestic industrial capacity for both incumbent primes and newer defense companies.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Hadrian is a leading private bet on reindustrialization and defense production. Its funding demonstrates the scale of capital moving into companies that pair automation with hard manufacturing capacity.

changed.text: Raised $260M in Series C financing and expanded its California and Arizona factory footprint.
Raised $1.37B in Series D funding at a valuation just shy of $8B.

takeaways: Hadrian's value proposition is domestic production speed and reliability, not software alone.
Defense demand gives the company a strategic customer base but introduces complex qualification cycles.
Factory utilization and execution against expansion plans are the primary risks.
